title: Profile Pack Rollout SLO Guardrails (Latency, Errors, Canary Escalation)
author: Sean Gallagher
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the **SLO guardrails** and **escalation/rollback criteria** for rolling out changes to the Serving Runtime **hardware tuning profiles pack** (kernel selection + scheduler/batching + KV cache/memory knobs).

The goal is to enable profile improvements while preventing:
- **Tail-latency regressions** (especially p99) under mixed workloads
- **Increased error rates** (OOM, timeouts, 5xx)
- **Silent degradation** (kernel fallbacks, fragmentation growth) that may not show up immediately in aggregate latency

These guardrails apply to:
- **Hosted**: Redwood-controlled fleet, staged rollout required
- **Dedicated**: opt-in rollout required; stronger customer-visibility requirements
- **Private**: guidance/validation requirements (no auto-rollout), compatibility gate required

## Definitions
**Profile change**: Any change that can affect serving behavior, including:
- Changing default profile selection rules
- Changing any profile knob defaults (batching, queueing, concurrency limits, KV cache headroom, compaction thresholds)
- Changing kernel selection ordering/fallback thresholds

**Control cohort**: Hosts/pools remaining on previous default profile version during canary.

**Treatment cohort**: Hosts/pools receiving new profile version.

**Workload mix**: All production routes/models served by a cohort. For Hosted canaries, cohorts must be selected to include a representative mix (chat + embeddings if applicable, short/long prompts, streaming/non-streaming).

**SLO windows** (defaults unless service has a stricter SLO):
- **Fast detection window**: 30–60 minutes
- **Stability window**: 24 hours
- **Error budget window**: 7 days (rolling)

## Required capabilities before any rollout
Rollout is blocked unless all items below are true.

### 1) Control-plane and runtime safety controls
- Kill switch must exist to disable profile pack defaults (Hosted).
- Runtime must report **active profile_id** and **profile_version** via:
  - Startup log summary
  - /health (or debug endpoint) field(s) used by on-call
- Rollback must be possible by **reverting default profile_version** (preferred) without requiring a runtime binary rollback.
- Dedicated must support **customer profile_version pinning** with auditability (who/when/why) and safe constraints.

### 2) Observability readiness (dashboards + tags)
The following tags/labels are required on core metrics:
- sku (H100/B200/L40S + form factor when available)
- profile_id
- profile_version
- model (or model_family) and route where cardinality allows (see dashboard spec)

Required dashboards (must exist and be linked in the rollout ticket/runbook):
1. **Runtime Profiles – Overview**
   - Adoption by profile_version (hosts, traffic)
   - Latency p50/p95/p99 by profile_version
   - Kernel fallback counters/rate by profile_version
2. **Request Latency Breakdown**
   - End-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99)
   - Queueing time (scheduler_queue_ms) (p50/p95/p99)
   - Compute time split (prefill vs decode) when available
3. **Error & Saturation**
   - 5xx rate, timeouts, cancellations
   - OOM events (GPU OOM + allocator OOM)
   - Admission control drops / backpressure signals
4. **Memory/KV Cache Health**
   - Fragmentation estimate, compaction time, compaction frequency
   - KV cache hit rate (if available) and eviction pressure
5. **Kernel Selection / Fallback**
   - kernel_choice distribution
   - kernel_fallback_rate with breakdown by reason

## Rollout stages (Hosted)
Unless otherwise approved by SRE on-call lead, Hosted rollouts use the following stages:

### Stage 0: Perf-canary / benchmark-lab gate (pre-prod)
Entry criteria:
- Benchmark matrix run completed for affected SKUs
- Acceptance thresholds met (see benchmark matrix page)
- No new “allowed-to-fail” gaps introduced without explicit sign-off

Exit criteria:
- Benchmarks show improvements or neutral changes within thresholds
- Any regressions are explained, scoped, and accepted by Runtime + SRE

### Stage 1: Production canary (≤ 1% traffic per region)
Duration: minimum 60 minutes, extend to 24h if traffic is low or metrics are noisy.

Cohort selection:
- At least one cohort per primary region
- Include mixed prompt-length workloads (short + long context) and at least one high-concurrency customer workload if available

### Stage 2: Expand canary (5% → 25%)
Duration: minimum 4 hours at 5%, then 24 hours at 25%.

### Stage 3: General availability (100%)
Rollout proceeds region-by-region unless traffic is global-balanced and cohorts are clearly isolated.

## Guardrails (what blocks rollout)
Guardrails below are evaluated against:
- Control cohort (previous profile) AND
- Rolling baseline (last 7 days, same hour-of-day if possible)

Unless noted, thresholds apply per region and globally. If any region trips a rollback trigger, pause global expansion.

### A) Latency guardrails (primary)
Latency guardrails focus on **p95 and p99**, with additional checks for queueing time to detect scheduler regressions.

**Block expansion** (do not move to next stage) if any of the following are true for ≥ 30 minutes:
- **End-to-end p95** increases by **> 8%** vs control cohort for the same route/model_family AND absolute delta is **> 15 ms** (whichever is larger).
- **End-to-end p99** increases by **> 5%** vs control cohort AND absolute delta is **> 25 ms**.
- **scheduler_queue_ms p99** increases by **> 20%** vs control cohort OR exceeds an absolute threshold:
  - Hosted default: **queue p99 > 40 ms** sustained (indicates overload/queue policy issue)

**Rollback** (revert profile_version / disable profile pack default) if any of the following are true for ≥ 10 minutes:
- End-to-end **p99 increases by > 10%** vs control cohort (any route/model_family) AND is sustained after accounting for traffic shifts.
- Queueing **p99 > 75 ms** sustained in canary cohort (strong indicator of scheduler regression or insufficient admission control).
- A “tail blow-up” pattern is observed: stable p50/p95 but **p99 spikes with increased queueing** correlated to canary cohort only.

Notes:
- Tail regression assessment must consider request size buckets. A known acceptable trade-off must be documented in the “expected behavior” page for the SKU.
- If only one model family regresses and traffic can be safely routed away, Runtime may apply a scoped mitigation (routing policy / per-model override) with SRE approval.

### B) Error-rate guardrails (hard stop)
Errors are evaluated as rates over total requests, and must be segmented by sku and profile_version.

**Immediate rollback** if any of the following occur and are attributable to the new profile (even with small sample sizes):
- **GPU OOM** event rate exceeds **0.02%** of requests in canary cohort OR any burst of OOMs that causes customer-visible failures.
- **HTTP 5xx** increases by **> 0.05 percentage points** absolute vs control cohort for ≥ 10 minutes.
- **Timeouts** increase by **> 0.03 percentage points** absolute vs control cohort for ≥ 10 minutes.
- **Model load failures** (startup/model reload) increase in canary cohort (indicates compatibility mismatch or profile selection bug).

**Block expansion** (pause and investigate) if:
- 5xx increases by **> 0.02 percentage points** absolute vs control cohort for ≥ 30 minutes.
- Retries/cancellations increase by **> 15%** vs control cohort (often correlates with queueing or headroom issues).

### C) Kernel fallback / compatibility guardrails
Kernel fallback is treated as a leading indicator for performance and stability drift (wrong kernel chosen, driver/CUDA mismatch, unsupported attention path).

**Block expansion** if:
- kernel_fallback_rate increases by **> 2x** vs control cohort for ≥ 30 minutes, even if latency is flat.

**Rollback** if:
- kernel_fallback_rate increases by **> 5x** vs control cohort for ≥ 10 minutes OR
- Any fallback reason indicates an **unsupported** / **unsafe** execution path (e.g., missing required kernel variant, incompatible driver/CUDA).

### D) Memory/KV cache fragmentation guardrails
Fragmentation and compaction issues may manifest as gradual tail latency degradation and eventual OOMs.

**Block expansion** if:
- compaction_time_ms p95 increases by **> 30%** vs control cohort for ≥ 1 hour, or
- fragmentation_estimate increases monotonically in canary cohort for ≥ 4 hours while control is stable.

**Rollback** if:
- Any fragmentation/allocator signal crosses an “unsafe” threshold defined for the SKU in its expected behavior page AND is correlated with increased OOM risk (e.g., rising allocation failures, repeated compaction spikes).

## Canary escalation criteria (who/when)
### Paging vs ticketing
**Page SRE on-call + Runtime DRI** when:
- Any rollback condition is met
- Any customer-visible incident begins (SLO breach risk)
- OOMs begin occurring in the canary cohort
- Kernel fallback rate spikes with an unknown reason

**File an investigation ticket** (no page) when:
- Expansion is blocked due to mild guardrail failures (e.g., p95 > 8% but not sustained)
- Dashboard signals are noisy/inconclusive and require longer observation

### Escalation roles
- **SRE on-call lead**: go/no-go decision for stage progression; triggers rollback when guardrails are met.
- **Runtime DRI** (Scheduling/Kernel/KV cache depending on regression): triage, mitigation, and post-rollback follow-up.
- **Infra DRI**: validates fleet/driver/CUDA variance and ensures canary cohort integrity.

## Dedicated rollouts (customer-facing)
Dedicated is **opt-in** for any default profile_version change unless a customer contract explicitly allows “managed performance updates.”

Required before enabling for a customer:
- Customer notified (or internal CS owner aligned) with:
  - What changes (profile_version)
  - How to rollback (pin previous profile_version)
  - Expected behavior/trade-offs for their SKU
- A named internal owner for the change window

Dedicated guardrails:
- Use the same rollback triggers as Hosted, but with stricter operational posture:
  - Any p99 regression reported by the customer or visible in their Dedicated dashboards triggers immediate rollback unless the customer explicitly accepts.

## Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)
Private deployments do not auto-roll forward. Guardrails here define what we require in docs and validation.

Requirements:
- Installer must warn/refuse unsupported driver/CUDA + selected profile_version combinations.
- Docs must include:
  - Supported SKUs + driver/CUDA baseline
  - How to validate profile selection
  - How to pin/rollback profile_version

Recommended customer validation:
- Run the benchmark matrix subset for their primary models/workload sizes.
- Monitor kernel fallback + memory fragmentation for at least 24 hours under representative load.

## Rollback procedure (Hosted)
Rollback is executed by SRE on-call lead (or delegate) and must be reversible and auditable.

1) Disable new default profile_version / flip kill switch to revert to last known-good defaults.
2) Confirm cohort traffic shifts back to control profile_version.
3) Validate within 10–20 minutes:
   - p99 returns to baseline
   - queueing drops
   - error rates normalize
4) Capture the following in the incident/issue:
   - profile_version attempted
   - sku(s) impacted
   - first metric to trip and timestamps
   - suspected knob (batching/queueing/kernel/KV)

## Post-rollout requirements
Within 48 hours of completing Stage 3:
- Runtime must publish a short changelog entry summarizing:
  - New default profile_version
  - Material knob changes and expected behavior
  - Any known risks/mitigations
- SRE must ensure alert thresholds for kernel_fallback_rate and scheduler_queue_ms remain tuned (avoid alert fatigue).

## Appendix: Metrics used for gating (names are illustrative)
- request_latency_ms{profile_version,sku,route,model_family} (histogram)
- scheduler_queue_ms{profile_version,sku} (histogram)
- http_5xx_rate{profile_version,sku,route}
- request_timeout_rate{profile_version,sku,route}
- gpu_oom_count{profile_version,sku}
- allocator_oom_count{profile_version,sku}
- kernel_fallback_rate{profile_version,sku,kernel_family,reason}
- kernel_choice{profile_version,sku,kernel_variant}
- kv_compaction_time_ms{profile_version,sku} (histogram)
- fragmentation_estimate{profile_version,sku} (gauge)

## Owners
- Primary owner: **SRE** (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes)
- Runtime DRIs: **Scheduling** (Sofia Ivanova), **Kernel** (Hiro Tanaka), **KV cache/memory** (Omar El-Sayed)
- Dashboards/metrics: **Allison Grant** (with Observability ingestion support)
